title: I WON! Japanese Boomers on HARAKIRI Watch (Victory Q&A)
summary: He recounts winning his months-long copyright fight against a Japanese company (later removed from Content ID) and a thumbnail-art claimant, then answers viewer questions on his schedule and work ethic, careers, friendship, fiction, competing in natural bodybuilding, black-pill thinking, aliens, his grandfather, self-defense and the vaccine. Lifting content centres on why he won't compete and why bodybuilding needs mental depth.
claims: A Japanese company struck his anime videos for about five months and ignored counterclaims even through a hired translator; he risked fighting legally rather than surrender his freedom of speech
He won back one video after three months; when the company re-blocked it, YouTube found the block illegal and removed the company from the copyright ID system, restoring all his videos
A second claimant over a drawing used in a thumbnail backed off once he sent a lawyer-drafted challenge
He would rather go to the past than the future; progress without looking back repeats past mistakes
Training footage should be short recaps with voice-over explaining methods, not entertainment that replaces your own drive to train
To make friends as an adult, target other people who also lack friends and actively seek them out, even as an introvert; build hobbies that put you among new people
If he writes a book it will be free heroic fantasy fiction with themes such as masculine archetypes
Self-employment means total responsibility with no safety net; he prefers selling his time to a company and clocking out at 5 PM
Don't seek fulfillment in your job; earn money there and develop yourself in the time outside it; his passion is lifting
His day: up at 8, work 8:30-5:30, gym about 6:20-9 PM, family time, then video work 10 PM-1 AM; roughly 50 h work, 20 h training and 10-15 h content per week
His work ethic comes from immigrant parents who instilled discipline; his struggle is not doing too much, as he burnt out working 60-80 h weeks
He allows himself 15-30 minutes of idle time daily but too much depresses him
Medieval peasants worked about half the year; the Industrial Revolution turned people into worker ants and today's mass quitting is the pendulum swinging back
Unskilled jobs will be automated; jobs tending the machines are the safe bet, which is why he works in tech
Use the 'monkey branch' career strategy: no loyalty to companies, get raises by bringing competing offers, and jump between companies
Subscriber program reviews stopped because the programs were all the same and taught nothing new; a new format is planned
In Hunter x Hunter Nen terms he looks like a conjurer from outside but is really a manipulator: logical, argumentative, does things his own way
Revolutions are typically a shadow class manipulating commoners to remove a rival elite; watch who is funding the rioters
His favorite fiction is a French young-adult fantasy series by an author who died young in a motorcycle accident; he ranks it with Lord of the Rings and far above Harry Potter
His favorite film is Watchmen for its gray morality, and One Piece is to him the greatest story ever told
He won't enter tested natural shows until testing can detect past drug use, because he refuses to compete against cheaters
Stage conditioning is pointless; the ideal is the 12-16% body fat look of early 20th-century bodybuilders, and he'd be judged too fat at 14%
Natural bodybuilding should be a one-man show posed in nature, not under stage lights with fake tan
He doesn't know how to pose and won't teach posing, tanning or peaking
You can't get advanced at anything at face value; lifters who see bodybuilding as just lifting heavy either turn to drugs or stay stuck, because their understanding has plateaued
Natural Hypertrophy aims to grow both mind and body; bodybuilding is more a spiritual practice than a physical one
If you're black-pilled, leave image boards and stop watching the news; elite boogeymen have no real impact on your life and blaming them dodges responsibility
Aliens are logically possible, but humans depict them in their own image; he'll believe when one beats his deadlift PR
His grandfather, in his early 90s, still swings a chainsaw and slaughters pigs, proving physical activity is the pinnacle of health; he also built houses himself
Self-defense is a human right; your property extends your body, and any force against someone who attacks you is appropriate; he moved to a country that allows it
Disarming law-abiding citizens only removes their protection, since criminals don't follow laws
The 'weak' a man protects are women, children and the elderly; healthy people at very low risk need not sacrifice their bodily freedom for others while society ignores its own health
He declined the vaccine, hasn't gotten sick, and says you must live by your own principles rather than submit to something you may regret
